# TaaSFlow — full text of canonical pages

> TaaSFlow is a recruiting platform with managed execution. Agents source and score candidates. A recruiter reviews every shortlist before you see it. You make every hiring decision.

## TaaSFlow — recruiting platform with managed execution — https://taasflow.com/

What the service is and who it is for.

- Each requirement points to the line in the CV or application that supports it, so you can check the reasoning.
- Your team reviews candidates, compares them and moves them forward in one place.
- A recruiter reviews every shortlist before it reaches you. Your team runs the interviews and decides who to hire.
- Roles at hotels, restaurants, resorts and event venues.
- Clinical, administrative and leadership roles where credentials matter.
- Roles you fill in numbers, such as retail and store teams.
- TaaSFlow helps your team find and evaluate candidates, with recruiting execution and a shared workspace to review the evidence. Your team keeps control of interviews and hiring decisions.
- A shortlist you can check, not a stack of CVs.
- Four steps from role brief to shortlist.
- Enter your own salary, agency fee and hiring volume. Every starting value is an editable example, not an industry average.

## How it works — https://taasflow.com/how-it-works

Intake, sourcing, screening, shortlist, hire.

- Four steps from your hiring brief to a ranked shortlist: share the role, approve the plan, sourcing and screening, then review the evidence behind each score.
- From your hiring brief to a ranked shortlist.
- A hiring team reviewing candidate shortlists together at a table
- The intake becomes an approved blueprint.
- Your intake is not filed away — it becomes the scoring rubric, the search plan, and the screening spec. Weights and deal-breakers are approved before sourcing starts.
- Must-haves, nice-to-haves, and deal-breakers made explicit
- Search plan reviewed with you before launch
- Named-target outreach, our own talent network and past finalists come first
- Universities, partners, referrals, events and press when a role warrants it
- Whatever the channel, the candidate is scored on the same rubric
- Every score has a quote. Every quote has a source.
- Before you see a shortlist, a recruiter reviews each candidate against the rubric and checks the evidence behind every requirement. A requirement that cannot be evidenced is flagged, not hidden.
- Recruiter-approved before it reaches your workspace
- Match / partial / gap called honestly per requirement
- Fit narrative written by a human, not a template
- Adjust the rubric weights and watch the order change. In your real workspace weights are approved at intake — this demo lets you see how the model reacts.
- You interview fewer people, and better ones.
- The delivery is a workspace — not a PDF.
- Candidates arrive in a workspace you and your TaaSFlow recruiter share. Stage moves are validated, threads are scoped per role, and every decision is recorded next to the candidate it applies to.
- A model this transparent only works if roles are clear. Here is exactly who owns each step — us, you, or both.
- Request the pilot for one role, or book a call to talk it through first.
- Already have a job description? Go straight to the full intake.
- Example engagements and how we measure them.
- How teams at different stages use TaaSFlow.

## Platform — https://taasflow.com/platform

The ATS and workspace clients work in.

- No candidate reaches your shortlist until evidence is verified and the release is approved.
- Each score names the rubric version it ran on. Versions are frozen once scored against.
- Weights, must-haves and intensity — steady, standard or aggressive — are set per role.
- Every state change, override, release and access event is appended, never edited.
- Escalation path to a recruiter inside the workspace.
- Hire, reject or withdrawal — with the reason captured at decision time.
- The verified evidence behind that outcome stays attached to the record.
- What worked and what to avoid is kept as notes against the role family.
- New rubrics resurface past candidates and inherit role memory, so briefing starts ahead.
- Doesn't source, doesn't score, doesn't produce a shortlist.
- Often leaves no system behind, so the pipeline can go with the vendor.
- Doesn't run intake, doesn't score against a rubric, doesn't hand off to hiring.
- Doesn't produce ranked, evidenced shortlists on active roles.
- Requirements enter once, compile into a versioned rubric, and every step after that is recorded.
- An operations lead reviewing hiring performance on a wall display in a modern office
- Representative data for one senior platform role. In the workspace this is the real record, with reviewer history attached.
- Every shortlist arrives with the evidence that produced it.
- Request the pilot for one role and see the rubric, the agent runs and your first evidence-backed shortlist in your workspace.
- Pick a module. See exactly what it does.
- What enters it, what it does, what it produces, what you control, and what gets recorded.
- Requirement, evidence, source, rule, points, decision. Pick a requirement and follow the whole chain. Where evidence is missing, it says so.
- A role moves through working stages, and each one names its owner, its outputs and what is blocking it. Decisions sit next to the evidence.
- People stay in the loop as governance — approving, escalating and overriding, with each action logged.
- Each closed role makes the next one shorter.
- Not a model that trains itself. Verified outcomes, retained evidence and role memory that your next rubric can read.
- Retained data stays inside your organisation. You can edit or remove any record, and every re-engagement is logged.
- Adjacent categories, and the gap they leave.
- Runs the whole loop — intake, rubric, agents, evidence, scoring, decisions and memory — in one system you keep.

Engagement outcomes. Client names are withheld unless a client approved attribution.

- Examples of how a TaaSFlow engagement runs, using representative example data. Not reported client results.
- Deep dives on hiring economics and evaluation.
- No quote is published for an example engagement. We publish a testimonial only when a client has written it and approved it for attribution.
- Hiring metrics are easy to mix up, so these are the definitions we use. When a figure is published on this site, it states where it comes from.
- Accepted offers divided by offers extended.
- A different ratio: hires divided by shortlisted candidates. It measures shortlist quality, not the strength of an offer, and it should not be compared with offer acceptance.
- Six example engagements across hospitality, finance, healthcare, technology, consumer and industrial hiring. They show how a search runs from brief to shortlist.

## FAQ — https://taasflow.com/faq

Billing, scope, screening and data questions.

- What TaaSFlow is, how the system runs a search, and where expert oversight sits.
- A hiring operating system. You submit roles through a structured intake, our delivery team runs sourcing and screening, and candidates are delivered inside a shared workspace with evidence against every requirement.
- Think of it as hiring infrastructure you subscribe to: agents run the search, evidence backs every score, and expert oversight approves what reaches you — the same workspace and the same context across every role you run.
- How is TaaSFlow different from an agency?
- You get a workspace instead of a PDF, a flat subscription instead of placement fees, and evidence instead of a verdict. Delivery is not contingent on placement.
- A dedicated TaaSFlow team handles intake, sourcing, screening, and evidence capture. Your hiring managers keep decision rights end-to-end.
- No. TaaSFlow runs the pre-hire workflow inside its own workspace and hands over into your ATS at the point you decide.
- Yes. Most clients start with one or two roles to see how delivery works before scaling. Pilot scope and cadence are agreed together.
- Flat subscription, no placement fees, and how the commercial model works in practice.
- A flat monthly subscription. No placement fees, no per-hire commissions. The subscription covers sourcing, screening, evidence, and workspace delivery for the roles in scope.
- Tiers scale by concurrent role volume. You can pause, resize, or add roles between billing cycles — the workspace and history stay intact.
- No. Delivery is not contingent on placement, so there is no incentive to push weak candidates.
- Monthly, on the terms agreed with your account team and documented in your contract.
- The Pricing page shows tiers and typical monthly ranges. Exact scope is confirmed in the commercial conversation.
- How candidates surface, what evidence you receive, and how volume is calibrated.
- They surface in your workspace as a ranked shortlist, each with evidence mapped against the requirements defined in the brief.
- Shortlists are sized to the role and the market. We favour signal over volume — usually a small, hand-reviewed shortlist per cadence rather than a firehose.
- Yes. Feedback in the workspace shapes the next batch. You can also open new requirement variants without restarting the intake.
- Evidence-first evaluation and how disagreements are resolved.
- Each requirement in the brief is scored against concrete evidence — experience, projects, credentials, or answers to screening questions. Reviewers always see the evidence, not just a verdict.
- Structured tooling supports the delivery team, but a human reviews evidence before a candidate ever surfaces to a client.
- Assisted, not automated. AI supports evidence extraction and ranking, but a human recruiter signs off before delivery.
- Feedback inside the workspace goes straight to the delivery team and recalibrates the next batch.
- Can we see the reasoning behind a score?
- Yes — every candidate carries per-requirement evidence and a rationale. Nothing is a black box.
- Access, visibility, collaboration, and what the workspace does day-to-day.
- Your client account, invited teammates, and the TaaSFlow delivery team assigned to your roles. No wider distribution.
- Can multiple teammates review candidates?
- Open roles, current stage per candidate, feedback exchanged, and messages — in one live view. No status meetings required.
- Yes. Messaging is inside the workspace so it stays attached to the role, not lost in email threads.
- Multi-team scale, governance, reporting, and enterprise access controls.
- Does TaaSFlow support multiple teams or business units?
- Yes. Enterprise accounts run parallel searches across teams and business units on a shared workspace with account-level reporting.
- Do you support SSO and enterprise access controls?
- Enterprise access, provisioning, audit logs, and security details are agreed on a 20-minute call.
- Account-level reporting rolls up roles across teams, with role-level detail available in each requisition. TA, Finance, and Procurement each get views tailored to their questions.
- How do we start an enterprise engagement?
- Book a 20-minute call and we'll scope it with your TA and Procurement leads.
- Staffing and recruiting agencies using TaaSFlow to scale delivery.
- Yes. TaaSFlow partners with staffing and recruiting agencies who want more delivery capacity while keeping the client relationship.

- Try a broader query, clear filters, or contact us — we may serve the vertical without a dedicated page yet.

- We build custom rubrics for adjacent sectors.
- Tell us what you hire for. We'll confirm coverage, share a sample rubric, and start a role if it's a fit.

## Privacy — https://taasflow.com/privacy

How candidate and client data is handled.

- How TaaSFlow collects, uses, and protects personal information across recruitment activities.
- How TaaSFlow collects, uses, and protects personal information.
- Personal data collected through the intake, application, and workspace flows is stored in a managed Postgres database, with the application served from an edge hosting network. CV files are held in private object storage with row-level access policies. The named providers behind this infrastructure are listed in the sub-processor register in section 6 below.

## Agents — https://taasflow.com/agents

The agents that run a search, with their inputs, outputs and approval gates.

- Agents keep working between your meetings — inside limits you set.
- Share a role and choose which agents run.
- You choose which agents run, what they may send, and what must be approved before a candidate reaches you.
- Agents do not talk in prose. Each one passes a structured record forward, and the Governance Agent records the handoff.
- Approval gates sit between the blueprint and sourcing, and between scoring and release. Work stops at those gates until a person clears it.
- This is the activity rail from the workspace: actor, action, time, status and result — including the runs that are waiting on a person.

## Enterprise — https://taasflow.com/enterprise

Security, procurement, seats and audit requirements for larger programmes.

- Recruiting with managed execution for teams hiring at volume: ranked, evidence-backed shortlists, access controls and audit trails in one workspace.
- Recruiting infrastructure for teams running many roles at once: recruiting agents, multichannel outreach, evidence-backed scoring, governance controls and audit trails in one workspace.
- One or two functions hiring in parallel with shared standards.
- Agent capacity plus a named account lead
- Multi-business-unit hiring with executive reporting.
- Twice-weekly delivery across the portfolio
- Portfolio hiring across teams in one package.
- A continuous hiring programme run as one package.
- Continuous hiring where volume shifts by quarter.
- No search starts until must-haves, nice-to-haves and weightings are signed off in writing at intake.
- Each score line carries the source text it came from, so a hiring committee can check the reasoning.
- A recruiter reviews every shortlist before you see it. You make every hiring decision.
- Change the brief and affected candidates are flagged for re-review rather than left on a stale score.
- Consistent rubric across every role family
- The same role family is scored against the same rubric version, whichever recruiter runs the search.
- Advance, hold and pass all require a reason code, which feeds calibration for the next batch.
- UK, EU-27, EFTA and select MENA markets, with local time-zone screening and language filters.
- North America, LATAM and the Caribbean, with time-zone-aligned pipelines for cross-region teams.
- Australia, New Zealand, India, Singapore and Southeast Asia, with explicit local-hours filters.
- Every account is isolated at the database layer. Your candidates and pipelines are never visible to another tenant.
- Access is scoped to business unit, team or requisition, and candidate contact details are released deliberately, not by default.
- Candidates apply directly and consent to processing. CVs are stored in private storage with time-limited access links.
- Score changes, decisions, releases and exports are logged with actor and timestamp for internal review.
- DPAs, sub-processor lists, retention windows and security questionnaires are completed during onboarding.
- Role families, business units, expected volume, stakeholders and reporting needs.
- Business units, hiring teams, permissions and dashboards configured to match your org.
- Criteria and weightings approved per role family. Agent capacity assigned and oversight briefed.
- Calibration on the first batches, then a standing review on volume, quality and cycle time.
- Roles live in different spreadsheets, ATSes, and inboxes. Nobody has a single view of what is actually happening.
- Every recruiter scores differently. Hiring managers see different signals for what is supposedly the same role.
- Batches of résumés arrive without evidence. Decisions rely on trust rather than what the CV actually says.
- TA leads, business partners, and hiring managers all need context — and end up reconstructing it in status meetings.
- Interviews start with no shared record of what was assessed at sourcing, so questions get repeated and time is lost.
- Cycle time and stage health are calculated retroactively from stale exports rather than a live account view.
- Business units, teams, and hiring managers modeled explicitly so requisitions, permissions, and reporting line up with how you actually operate.
- Agent capacity aligned to each role family or business unit. Standards stay consistent as volume changes and new requisitions open.
- Every open role is a separate pipeline inside the same Client workspace — no context switching between tools per requisition.
- Requisition portfolio view for TA leadership
- Role-scoped pipelines for hiring managers
- Business-unit rollups for people partners

## Trust — https://taasflow.com/trust

Commitments on data, screening and how decisions are recorded.

- The commercial trust pack for TaaSFlow. How pricing works, what you keep, how scoring works, candidate privacy, and where the line runs between TaaSFlow and your team.
- Your role blueprints, rubrics, screening questions, and scoring logic.
- Every decision, comment, and hire record, with a history of who changed what.
- Exportable shortlists and share links for internal stakeholders.
- Every score points at a specific line in the CV, an answer to a screening question, or a piece of enrichment data. If we cannot cite it, we do not score it.
- The scoring rubric is generated from your role blueprint — must-haves, preferred criteria, dealbreakers, and screening answers. It is visible to you before any candidate is scored.
- Once a score is generated it is written to an append-only record with the model version and the evidence used. Nobody can rewrite history.
- When two evidence sources disagree — CV vs LinkedIn, claim vs screening answer — we flag it as a contradiction on the candidate card instead of picking a winner.
- Every extracted fact carries a confidence signal. Low-confidence facts do not carry the same weight as verified ones and are visible as such.
- Candidates can request access, correction, and deletion at any time.
- CVs are stored in a private bucket with per-organization access, encrypted at rest.
- External stakeholder share links are token-gated, scoped to the shortlist, and revocable.
- The AI models used for CV parsing and role-fit scoring are named in the sub-processor register of the privacy notice.
- Consent and legal basis are recorded per candidate — with a full history of every access.
- We help translate the ask into a structured brief and rubric.
- You approve the brief, the rubric, and the dealbreakers before sourcing starts.
- We run multi-channel sourcing and outreach with delivery health tracking.
- You see the pipeline in real time and can pause, redirect, or comment.
- We parse CVs, extract evidence, and score against your rubric.
- You review, override, and decide. Every override is captured with a reason.
- We deliver a ranked shortlist with evidence and provenance.
- You decide who moves forward. We never make hire/no-hire calls for you.
- We host the system of record and keep the full change history complete.
- What happens if we stop working with TaaSFlow?
- No. Pricing is package-based and published above. Higher volume gets a lower cost per role. Enterprise plans are custom but never percentage-based.
- Do candidates know they are being evaluated by an AI-assisted system?
- Yes. The application flow and privacy notice make the AI-assisted evaluation explicit. Every evaluation is reviewable and reversible by a human.
- Can the AI make a hire or reject a candidate?
- How are you different from an ATS or a recruiting agency?
- An ATS stores. An agency executes. TaaSFlow is a recruiting execution system: system of record + sourcing + evidence-first scoring + live client control + persistent memory across roles.
- TaaSFlow runs alongside — the system of record for how the role was actually run, the evidence behind every candidate, and the memory that carries between roles.
- In an isolated, per-organization workspace with row-level security. Encrypted at rest. Access is scoped to your team and, when granted, our staff — every read is logged.
- Per-organization workspace with row-level security on every table.
- Least-privilege roles: platform admin, client admin, editor, viewer. All access audited.
- TLS in transit. Encrypted at rest. Private storage for CVs and evidence.
- Immutable audit events for score runs, decisions, and admin actions.
- Consent and legal basis recorded per candidate with a full change history.
- Candidates can request access, correction, or deletion. We honor them in-product.
- One-off packages, published prices, no percentages.
- Higher volume gets a lower cost per role. You never pay a percentage of salary. You never pay placement fees.

Contract terms for the subscription and pilot.
